No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result NCH: Nasarawa Hosts 1,000 Delegates As 67th council Opens In Lafia by Ahmed Tahir Ajobe 14 seconds ago in North Central , News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The 67th Regular National Council on Health (NCH) opened in Lafia, Nasarawa State, on Monday, with delegates charged to move Nigeria from health commitments to measurable results.
The council, holding from November 16 to 20, 2026, is themed: “From Commitment to Results: Delivering Quality and Equitable Healthcare for All Nigerians.”
It is the first time Nasarawa State will host the apex health policy-making body since its creation in 1996.
Over 1,000 delegates are attending the meeting, including commissioners for health from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), permanent secretaries, heads of agencies, directors and development partners.
Declaring the council open, the Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Ms Daju Kachollum, welcomed delegates and commended Governor Abdullahi A. Sule for hosting the meeting.
She said Nasarawa holds a special place in her heart, describing the state as home.
“I am very happy to be here in Nasarawa. Nasarawa is home to me. Nasarawa used to be part of Plateau State, so I call them our younger ones, even though they are excellent in what they do,” she said.
Kachollum said it was her honour and privilege to welcome delegates to the 67th NCH, expressing confidence that the technical session would do justice to the memos before it.
“I will not go ahead to read the proceedings here because His Excellency came to declare this open, and after he has declared it open, we will begin our technical session in earnest,” she said.
She thanked Nasarawa State for hosting the national health family on behalf of permanent secretaries from the states and the FCT, heads of agencies and directors.
She had earlier urged members of the Technical Committee and Sub-Committees to prioritise evidence, professionalism and measurable results in shaping recommendations for the health sector.
In his goodwill address, the Deputy Governor of Nasarawa State, Dr Emmanuel Akabe, commissioned the 1,000-seat ultramodern international event centre hosting the council.
He congratulated the Minister of Health and Nasarawa State for hosting the 67th council meeting.
Akabe described Nasarawa as a peaceful, accommodating and welcoming state.
He said Nasarawa means victory, while Lafia means wealth, adding that the state is blessed and produces food for the nation.
On the theme of the council, Akabe said there could be no better time to discuss delivering quality and equitable healthcare for all Nigerians.
He prayed that the outcome of deliberations and all resolutions would be implemented comprehensively.
He also celebrated the outgoing Permanent Secretary, noting that she served for 24 years in the Ministry of Health and left without blemish.
He thanked Governor Sule for the honour of declaring the 67th session open.
Earlier, the Commissioner for Health, Dr Gaza Gwamna, welcomed commissioners, directors, policymakers, members of the media and other delegates.
He described the gathering as an opportunity to take decisions that will benefit the people.
Gwamna urged participants, including permanent secretaries and commissioners, to take responsibility for one another, stressing that no one should suffer in silence.
He called for solidarity and hospitality, and invited delegates to enjoy the museum and other historical sites in the state.
He said the administration of Governor Sule has in the last seven years prioritised the health sector, with massive investments in infrastructure, comprehensive upgrade of hospitals and health facilities, and procurement of state-of-the-art medical equipment to improve access to quality healthcare, particularly maternal and child health.
He commended the Federal Government for granting the state the hosting right and assured that government would provide all necessary support to ensure a successful and hitch-free council meeting.
The council brings together key stakeholders across the federal and state health sectors to deliberate on memos and agree on policies to improve healthcare delivery in Nigeria.
